daily_reality.typical_workday: SLPs work 8-hour days in most settings, with some flexibility for part-time or school-based schedules. Day starts with reviewing patient files and schedules, followed by staff meetings to discuss appointments or medical complications. Core tasks: conducting screenings and evaluations of speech/language/swallowing disorders, delivering individual and group therapy sessions, writing treatment plans, documenting progress notes (SOAP format), attending IEP meetings in schools, consulting with teachers/physicians/families, and managing billing/Medicaid documentation. School-based SLPs manage caseloads of 40-80+ students; medical SLPs see 6-10 patients daily. Administrative duties consume 25-40% of the workday. Over 180,800 SLPs employed in the US (2023); projected to reach 214,100 by 2033.
deadlines: IEP annual reviews and triennial re-evaluations
State license renewal (varies by state, typically every 1-2 years)
ASHA CCC-SLP certification maintenance (30 PDHs per 3-year cycle)
daily_reality.seasonality: School-based SLPs follow the academic calendar with heavy evaluation periods in fall (September-October) and spring (March-April) for IEP meetings. Summer may offer reduced caseloads or extended school year (ESY) services. Medical settings maintain year-round demand. Flu season and stroke season (winter) increase hospital-based referrals. Back-to-school screenings spike in August-September. Medicare year-end therapy cap considerations in November-December.

regulatory.licensing: Master's degree from a CAA-accredited program required. Must complete 400+ supervised clinical practicum hours. Pass the Praxis Examination in Speech-Language Pathology (minimum score 162 for ASHA certification). Complete a 36-week Clinical Fellowship Year (CFY) with approximately 1,260 hours of professional experience. All 50 states and DC require state licensure. Five states (Alaska, Delaware, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Virginia) require CCC-SLP for state licensure. School-based SLPs may need an additional teaching license/certificate. ASHA CCC-SLP certification requires 30 Professional Development Hours (PDHs) per 3-year maintenance interval, including 1 PDH in ethics and 2 PDHs in culturally responsive services. Effective January 1, 2026, updated certification standards clarify professional development content areas. New 2027 Certification Standards in Speech-Language Pathology are being developed by ASHA.
regulatory.penalties: Practicing without a license: state-specific fines and potential criminal charges. HIPAA violations: up to $50,000 per incident. ASHA Code of Ethics violations: CCC-SLP revocation, public reprimand, or suspension. Medicare/Medicaid fraud: federal criminal prosecution, fines up to $50,000 per false claim. Failure to maintain continuing education: license suspension. Inadequate supervision of SLPAs: disciplinary action.

career_psychology.burnout: SLP burnout is driven by high caseloads (school SLPs average 50+ students, some exceeding 80), excessive paperwork consuming 25-40% of work time, productivity requirements in medical settings (often 85-90% billable), emotional toll of working with patients who have severe disabilities, and workplace isolation. School-based SLPs report highest burnout due to large varied caseloads and IEP meeting demands. Specialized SLPs experience less burnout due to focused practice areas. Hospital SLPs face burnout from varied and intense caseloads. Contributing factors include student loan debt ($60,000-$100,000+ for master's degree) relative to school-based salaries, lack of administrative support, and feeling undervalued by employers. Self-care strategies and specialization are key protective factors.
